compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc Pro B70/XPU Triton path should favor dense fp16 dot/DPAS-style tiles when possible; very small attention matrices may underutilize compute unless batched across many windows.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Total work is dominated by small-channel dense linear layers: qkv 32->96, proj 32->32, fc1 32->128, fc2 128->32 over 921600 tokens. Attention is many independent 16x16 softmaxes with C=32.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: If Triton XPU lowers small matrix shapes poorly, custom kernels may lose to torch.compile/GEMM libraries despite better fusion.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Eager reference materializes norm outputs, qkv, attention, projected activations, fc1 hidden, and fc2 outputs. Avoiding large fp16 intermediates, especially qkv and hidden MLP, is a major opportunity.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Full fusion can reduce traffic but may spill registers or duplicate weight reads; staged matmuls can be compute efficient but memory-heavy.

register_pressure.notes: Window size N=16 and C=32 are small enough for register-resident attention state, but holding q/k/v plus fc1 hidden=128 for multiple tokens can quickly exceed practical register budgets.
register_pressure.risk: Over-fusing norm, attention, projection, residual, LN2, GELU, and MLP can reduce occupancy and create spills.

nodes.notes:
1) Classification: mixed transformer block: small reductions for LayerNorm over C=32, dense fp16 linear layers, small-window attention/softmax over N=16, elementwise residual/GELU; accesses are dense NHWC except window reindexing is regular strided reshaping, not true sparse gather.
2) Canonical math: for each token x[b,h,w,32], LN1 reduces C, q/k/v are dense linear maps, each 4x4 window independently computes softmax((q/sqrt(32))kT + rpe) over 16 keys, applies v and proj, adds residual, then LN2, fc1 32->128, GELU, fc2 128->32, residual. Windows/tokens are independent except reductions within C or N.
3) Layout/access: input/output NHWC contiguous fp16, weights are PyTorch Linear layout [out,in], biases fp16, rpe_bias shape [1,1,16,16]. Dominant activation size is about 59 MB per 32-channel image; eager intermediates qkv and hidden MLP are much larger. Weights are tiny and reusable/cacheable.
4) Bottleneck regimes: large fixed image likely dense-linear compute plus intermediate memory traffic; small images/batches likely launch overhead; fully fused per-window path likely register/occupancy limited; staged GEMM path likely memory-bandwidth and kernel-launch limited; strict correctness path likely fp32 accumulation/softmax details dominate tolerance risk.
5) Design knobs: choose window-major vs token-tile mapping, degree of fusion, matmul tiling for small K=32/128, fp32 vs fp16 accumulation, where to materialize qkv/hidden, stable softmax strategy, number of tokens/windows per program, and specialization to B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32,N=16.
6) Skeleton: load tile/window, compute LN stats in fp32, apply affine, compute qkv, perform per-window QK softmax with rpe, apply V and projection, residual, compute LN2, MLP/GELU/fc2, final residual. Registers should hold LN stats and small attention rows; larger MLP hidden may require tiling/materialization. Synchronization should be within program only; windows are independent.
7) Candidate families: window-resident whole-block path minimizes memory but risks register pressure; dense-linear staged path maximizes hardware dot efficiency but writes intermediates; subgraph-specialized path targets attention and MLP separately with moderate fusion and lower implementation risk.

action.description: Implement a first Triton prototype organized around each 4x4 window: compute LN1, qkv, single-head attention with rpe, projection, first residual, then hand off to a second fused LN2+MLP pass or a minimal internal tiled MLP path.
action.rationale: The fixed N=16,C=32 window shape makes attention small enough to keep local state near registers and eliminates expensive qkv/attention window materialization. This has the highest upside if register pressure remains controlled.
action.title: Prototype window-resident Swin block path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Good fit for many independent windows, but individual 16x32 and 16x16 operations are small and may not fully utilize XPU matrix engines unless multiple windows are grouped per program.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Can reuse loaded window activations and small weights locally; attention arithmetic is modest, while linear layers still need efficient dot tiling.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: If per-window programs are too small, scheduling overhead and low vector utilization can offset memory savings.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Best chance to avoid materializing norm1, qkv, attention, and projected intermediates. Output traffic can approach reading input and writing final/partial residuals plus weights.
memory_bandwidth.risk: May need to spill or split MLP hidden, reintroducing global traffic.

register_pressure.notes: Holding x, normalized x, q/k/v, attention rows, projection accumulators, and possibly MLP partials for 16 tokens is demanding.
register_pressure.risk: Register spills and reduced occupancy are the primary limiter; a full-block single kernel may be too large.

nodes.notes: Intended regime: fixed large image with many 4x4 windows where reducing global intermediate traffic matters more than peak GEMM utilization. Strength: memory-minimal attention path. Weakness: complex correctness and register budgeting. SELF_CHECK: This sibling cannot be combined with the staged dense-linear sibling in the same first iteration because it chooses a different intermediate contract: qkv and attention are not materialized globally.

action.description: Build a conservative Triton baseline with separate kernels for LN/residual/GELU and custom tiled dense-linear operations for qkv, proj, fc1, and fc2, plus a compact batched 16x16 attention-softmax kernel.
action.rationale: Most FLOPs are in dense linears over 921600 tokens, so a GEMM-centered path has good hardware fit and lower correctness risk while still allowing targeted fusion around small reductions and elementwise operations.
action.title: Build dense-linear staged Triton baseline

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Likely the safest fit for Intel XPU matrix hardware because linears can be expressed as larger MxN tiles over a large token dimension with K=32 or K=128.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Dense fc1/fc2 dominate total operations and can amortize launch overhead over the full image. Attention remains small but is only a fraction of total work.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small K and fp16 accumulation policy may still limit achieved throughput versus vendor library kernels.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Writes qkv and fc1 hidden unless additional fusion is added. This increases traffic substantially but keeps kernels simple and compute-efficient.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Materializing qkv and hidden MLP can become the latency bottleneck for C=32 where arithmetic intensity is moderate.

register_pressure.notes: Lower pressure than full fusion because each kernel has a smaller live set. Matmul accumulators are controlled by tile size.
register_pressure.risk: Overly large output tiles or fusing too much epilogue into matmuls can still reduce occupancy.

nodes.notes: Intended regime: compute-dominated large images where robust fp16 dot throughput beats aggressive fusion. Strength: easiest path to correctness and stable performance. Weakness: high intermediate memory traffic and multiple launches. SELF_CHECK: This sibling cannot be combined with window-resident full fusion as an initial action because it explicitly materializes stage boundaries to prioritize dense matmul efficiency.

action.description: Implement two specialized Triton subgraphs: one for LN1+qkv+4x4 attention+proj+residual over windows, and one for LN2+fc1+GELU+fc2+residual over token tiles, with only the post-attention residual tensor shared between them.
action.rationale: This balances memory reduction and hardware utilization: attention can exploit fixed N=16 locality, while the MLP can use token-tiled dense computation without requiring a monolithic full-block kernel.
action.title: Prototype subgraph-specialized attention and MLP path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Better XPU fit than per-window monolith because the MLP subgraph can group many tokens, while attention remains specialized to the fixed 16-token window.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Separates the two natural computation domains: window-local attention and token-local MLP. This should preserve enough arithmetic intensity for fc1/fc2 while removing some eager overhead.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: The attention subgraph may still be too small-grained if not batched across windows effectively.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Avoids global qkv and attention matrices if attention subgraph is fused; may still materialize fc1 hidden depending on MLP tile strategy.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If fc1 hidden is written globally, memory traffic remains significant; if not, register pressure rises.

register_pressure.notes: Moderate pressure because fusion boundary after first residual prevents carrying all block state at once. MLP can tile hidden dimension rather than hold all 128 activations.
register_pressure.risk: Fusing LN2, fc1, GELU, and fc2 without materializing hidden requires careful accumulation and can increase live state.

nodes.notes: Intended regime: large image where both memory traffic and dot utilization matter. Strength: pragmatic split along natural residual boundary. Weakness: more implementation than staged baseline and less memory-minimal than full fusion. SELF_CHECK: This sibling cannot be combined with the other initial siblings because it commits to exactly one global boundary between attention and MLP, unlike fully staged or fully window-resident designs.

kernel_summary: This is a fixed-shape fp16 simplified Swin block over NHWC input [1,720,1280,32] with 57600 independent 4x4 windows, single-head N=16 attention, two LayerNorm reductions over C=32, dense linears 32->96, 32->32, 32->128, 128->32, GELU, and residuals. FLOPs are dominated by the dense MLP and qkv/proj linears, while PyTorch eager likely pays heavily for many materialized intermediates and layout/window reshapes. The best Triton strategy must balance XPU-friendly dense fp16 dot tiling against aggressive fusion to avoid global qkv/attention/hidden traffic, while preserving fp32-like LayerNorm/softmax accumulation accuracy and controlling register pressure for N=16,C=32,hidden=128.
open_questions: What correctness tolerance does the evaluator use for fp16 outputs, especially for LayerNorm variance, softmax, and GELU approximation differences?
Does Triton on Intel XPU for Arc Pro B70 generate efficient matrix-engine code for small K=32 and K=128 tl.dot shapes, or are hand-shaped smaller programs preferable?
Are model dimensions always exactly B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32,window=4x4,hidden=128, or must ModelNew handle other valid init shapes?
Is using torch operations for parameter initialization and non-kernel setup allowed as long as forward uses custom Triton kernels for the hot path?
How does the benchmark account for compilation/warmup and temporary allocation overhead on torch.xpu?
Are all Linear weights and biases contiguous in standard PyTorch [out,in] layout after state_dict loading, and is rpe_bias always pre-gathered as [1,1,16,16]?
What is the relative baseline: PyTorch eager only, torch.compile, or best of both, and what latency target is needed to score well?
